newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: British murder suspect's body identified.
newsitem.headline: British murder suspect's body identified.

text.p: The body of British murder suspect Clifford Harris, who drowned in the Swan River in Perth in Western Australia after eluding police, has been identified by his wife, police said on Thursday.
Harris, a 62-year-old retired teacher, was to be arrested in relation to the murder of a woman found in his abandoned pick-up truck on a farm in North Devon, Australian police said.
Police said an autopsy would be carried out on Thursday to determine the cause of Harris' death.
Janice Crompton, a 59-year-old art teacher, had lain for four days wrapped in a duvet tied with baler twine and placed in polythene bags in the rear of Harris' truck.
A bee hive, thought to belong to Harris, an amateur bee-keeper, had been placed on the body. British police believe Crompton was beaten to death last week.
British police are looking into the possibility that Harris and Crompton may have been having an affair.

Australian police said they had been asked by British police to find Harris and his wife Margaret, pending an arrest. The couple were located on January 28, but police were unable to make an arrest as the British warrant had not arrived.
The couple were placed under surveillance, but Clifford evaded police when he went for a walk on Wednesday. His body was later found near the Royal Perth Yacht Club.
His wife identified the body and has been interviewed by police and released, said Australian Federal Police spokesman Mick Duthie.
The British couple were believed to have arrived in Australia a few days ago on a two-month holiday, police said. The couple have a son living in Adelaide in South Australia.
